newsitem.title: USA: Cisco reports third quarter profits leap.
newsitem.headline: Cisco reports third quarter profits leap.

text.p: Computer networking leader Cisco Systems Inc. Tuesday reported sharply higher third quarter profits and revenues, but the figures fell short of Wall Street's highest expectations.

Cisco, which makes the gear that allows companies to connect computers to vast networks, reported a profit of $378.3 million or 55 cents a share in the three months ended in April, up from $245 million or 37 cents a year ago. Revenues rose 52 percent to $1.65 billion.
The latest quarter included a pretax gain of $32.3 million or 3 cents a share from the sale of a stock investment that on an after-tax basis.

Excluding the gain, Cisco's third-quarter profit was in line with analysts' consensus estimate of 52 cents a share, according to the First Call, which tracks estimates. In after-hours trading, however, Cisco stock slipped to $56 from an earlier close of $57.75 on Nasdaq, which was down $1.125 from Monday.

"The numbers they posted were consistent with the expectation level a week, but in the last few days the expectation level has been raised and the stock moved from the high 40s to the high 50s," one analyst said.

Analysts said revenues and expenses were in line with expectations, and that company executives in a conference call had discussed prospects of market weakness in Europe and Japan having bottomed out.
Analysts said the company described business having picked up in April after weaker-than-hoped-for business in February and March.

The results for Cisco, the nation's largest networking company, had been eagerly awaited by investors looking for an indication about whether the computer networking industry's rapid growth had started to cool down.
"We are pleased to report the 29th consecutive quarter of revenue and earnings growth, especially given our traditional third quarter challenges," Cisco President John Chambers said in a statement.

Earlier, Cisco and GTE Corp. also said they entered a strategic alliance to develop enhanced data and Internet services. Under the deal, GTE will buy networking equipment, such as switches and routers from Cisco. GTE said its purchases could reach more than $1 billion of Cisco products over the next five years.
